method: Flesch-Kincaid grade plus five using vowel-group syllable heuristic; pupil stage prompts, routes, goals, success, words and log; excludes staff guidance and optional stretch; estimate only, not a learner assessment.

lessons.pupil_corpus:
I can try a rubbing to show a feeling.
I can try the new way with help if I need it.
I can compare two tests.
I can choose one and say or show why.
You can point, speak, sign or watch first.
Pick a made-up feeling for your art.
Today we will try texture rubbing.
Look at a smooth surface and one with ridges.
Which has bumps?
You may look without touching.
Put safe card on the table.
Lay thin paper on top. Hold its edge.
Use the side of a crayon. Rub lightly.
Lift the paper. Look at the marks.
Help the adult make two tests.
Which marks can you see?
Choose a test for a made-up feeling.
Say: I chose ___ because ___.
In your book or arts log, choose a feeling.
Make two small texture tests.
Pick the test that fits your idea.
Keep both tests and your own reason.
Show the two tests to an adult.
Point to the texture you chose.
Say what you notice.
Tidy and keep the tests for next time.
Arts log: I tried ___.
My two tests were ___.
I chose ___ because ___.
Next time I will ___.
Pick a feeling or point to a choice.
Direct an adult through two small tests.
Choose one texture.
Say or show why you chose it.
Choose a made-up feeling.
Make two texture tests with the same crayon.
Pick the texture that fits your idea.
Keep both tests and your reason.
Complete the same two tests.
Try a lighter sweep on a small spare area.
Say what changes in the marks.
Choose a version for a reason.
The new way I tried was ___.
My two tests were ___.
My feeling or idea is ___.
I chose ___ because ___.
Next time I will ___.
texture
How a surface feels or looks.
rub
Move a tool back and forth.
light
With a small amount of force.
test
A small try before a piece.

I can use my new texture in a small piece.
I can use the new way I tried.
I can keep or change one part for a reason.
I can show what I did in my arts log.
Find the tests you made last time.
Point to the one you chose.
Today you can use it in a small piece.
Which texture did you choose?
What could it show in your piece?
You may keep your idea or change it.
Watch a small texture piece.
Put paper over the safe card.
Rub lightly in two small spaces.
Leave a gap. Check your idea.
Choose one texture for the class piece.
Where will it go?
Try one small change.
Keep or change it for a reason.
Make a small piece with your new texture.
Use your tests to help you choose.
Check one part. Keep it or change it.
Keep your work and your own reason.
Show one part you chose.
Say: I kept or changed ___ because ___.
You can share with just an adult.
Tidy your space.
Arts log: I tried the new way by ___.
I made ___.
I kept or changed ___ because ___.
Next I would ___.
Find or remake two small tests.
Choose a texture and direct the adult.
Make a small piece or silent sequence.
Show one choice and your reason.
Use your chosen texture in a small piece.
Check one feature against your idea.
Keep or change it for a reason.
Keep your work and dated arts-log entry.
Complete the same small piece.
Compare a first version with one small change.
Explain what the change does to the feeling.
Choose the version you want to keep.
The new way I used was ___.
My piece is about ___.
I made ___.
I kept / changed ___ because ___.
My real work or witness note is ___.
Next I would ___.

How a surface feels or looks.
rub
Move a tool back and forth.
light

I can start my piece from my own plan.
I can use my plan to start making.
I can explain a making decision.
I can record what I made and what changed.
Find your chosen Week 3 plan.
Say what your piece will show.
Choose a quiet way to work and share.
Check your tools, space and first step.
You have 14 minutes to make today.
What small part can you make in that time?
Look back at the plan before each step.
Make a small first section.
Check the feature that shows your idea.
Record one decision as you work.
Help check a first section against a plan.
What matches the intended idea?
Choose one small change if needed.
Say: I chose ___ because ___.
Use your Week 3 plan to make a first section.
Keep your chosen idea visible or clear in the sequence.
Pause once to check. Keep or change one feature.
Record your decision and the real next step.
Compare your work with the plan.
Ask for one useful observation.
Decide what you will keep or change next.
Store the work safely.
Arts log: I used my plan to make ___.
I decided ___ because ___.
I changed ___ from my plan because ___.
Next lesson I need to ___.
Read your plan with an adult.
Choose the first small section.
Make or direct it. Pause to check.
Say one choice and what comes next.
Check your plan and available tools.
Make the planned first section.
Keep or change one feature for a reason.
Log the real work, decisions and next step.
Complete the core making task.
Test two small versions of one feature.
Choose the version that fits your intention.
Keep the comparison and your reason.
My plan intended to show ___.
Today I actually made ___.
I decided ___ because ___.
I changed / kept ___ from my plan because ___.
The help or access method I used was ___.
My real next making step is ___.
resilience
Finding a way forward, with help or a change of plan.
intention
The idea or effect you want to show.
decision
A choice you make.
revise
Change part of a plan or piece.

Read the next step you chose.
Check what you can finish today.
Show the part that suggests resilience.

Look at the real first version.
Complete one planned part.
Check the effect. Try one small change.
Keep the version that fits your idea.

What effect does the change have?

Say what is really finished.
Use your next step to develop the piece.
Keep the idea clear in the work.
Check one feature. Keep it or change it for a reason.

Ask: What do you notice?
Check it against your intended idea.
Tidy and store the piece with your plan.
